edits.find_text: The fee starts a 30-day wait before any page can go live, and onboarding can take one to three weeks.
edits.new_text: The fee starts Steam's 30-day clock, and onboarding can take one to three weeks.
edits.reason: Unsupported and self-contradictory. Research 12 (line 20) says only 'a 30-day wait after paying the 100 dollar Steam Direct fee'; it never says the wait blocks the store page, and it lists the wait beside the two-week Coming Soon minimum and the 3 to 5 day page review as the runway before release. The doc's own plan pays the fee in Week 1 (29 September to 5 October) and puts the Coming Soon page live in Week 4 (20 to 26 October), which is inside 30 days, so 'before any page can go live' cannot be true at the same time as the Week 4 gate. Week 1 already uses the neutral wording 'so the 30-day clock runs'. partner.steamgames.com is blocked from this container, so the neutral wording is the one the research supports.

edits.find_text: and Google Play's sensitive-events policy bans appearing to profit from one unless the app is educational, documentary or artistic with a discernible benefit to the victims.
edits.new_text: and Google Play's sensitive-events policy bans appearing to profit from one with no discernible benefit to the victims, with an exception for educational, documentary or artistic content.
edits.reason: The doc fuses two separate conditions into one. Research 12 quotes the policy as banning 'appearing to profit from a sensitive event with no discernible benefit to the victims', with a separate exception for educational, documentary or artistic content. As written the doc requires both together, which overstates the bar.

edits.find_text: one real bang, and the minaret falls silent; blackout
edits.new_text: one real bang, and the minaret falls silent, so until Day 8 the adhan is one unaided voice from a roof; blackout
edits.reason: The new clause creates an unexplained gap. 'Faith is lived' says the adhan marks the phases of every day and 'The adhan is the clock' makes it the phase mechanic, but the minaret now falls silent on Day 3 and the Day 8 row says the speaker carries the adhan 'for the first time since the mosque was hit'. Days 4 to 7 would have no adhan and no clock. Research 11 proposed exactly this reconciliation (a neighbour calling the adhan from a roof unaided). The added clause is fiction, not a fact claim, so no verification file is needed.

The table has fourteen Quran entries but three of them (3:169-170, 76:8-9, 94:5-6) are two ayat each, so seventeen ayat; Ayat al-Kursi plus the three Quls are sixteen ayat, not four.
